messages:
alex: Heads up — planning thread for Q4 capacity + new enterprise onboards. We got a handful of contracts that start Nov 15 and the holiday surge + marketing campaign could overlap. Need a pragmatic bin-packing strategy that reduces fragmentation without raising latency for small low-cost tenants.

maria: +1. Can we quantify expected incremental GPU hours and peak concurrency? last forecast was fuzzy. :thinking_face:

capacity-bot: weekly forecast snapshot: baseline = 78k GPU hrs/mo, expected Q4 uplift = +22% (to ~95k), peak concurrency projection = +30% on 2026-11-24..2026-12-02.

sam: For context, a few enterprise workspaces will request pinned_capacity (dedicated pool) but still want burst. That increases fragmentation because we reserve whole nodes for low utilization.

kai: Proposal: introduce a small "insurance pool" (mixed-GPU micro-pool) sized for burst absorb + quick preempt; runs on cheaper quantized variants for cost. When enterprise pinned doesn't use reserved slots, we let micro-pool opportunistically pack smaller tenants there. Can fall back to dedicated if SLA requires.

jen: Sounds interesting. How do we avoid noisy-neighbor latency regressions when we mix heterogeneous VMs in the same rack?

alex: Two parts: scheduling + limits. Scheduler change: soft-affinity to avoid co-locating high-latency tenants with latency-sensitive ones. Limits: we cap shared slice per GPU (e.g., 25% max) and enforce per-tenant token-rate shaping.

sam: We should also add a fragmentation metric to the console: "wasted slots" (sum of free vram across allocated nodes where no fit exists). Right now we only track free GPUs, not internal VRAM gaps.

maria: Agree. Metric should break down by region and by GPU type (A100x4, H100-80, L40x2). APAC is tight on H100s; EU is constrained on A100.

capacity-bot: quick sim result (30-min run): with insurance pool = 4k hrs buffer and dynamic preempt, tail evictions drop 18%, but average packing efficiency falls 3% due to fragmentation on mixed racks.

kai: Trade-off seems ok if cost of missed SLAs > 3% extra infra. We can mitigate fragmentation by adding scheduled consolidation windows overnight where we drain low-priority workloads and compaction-migrate them.

jen: How long does a compaction migrate take? network egress and k-v cache warmup matter for large models.

sam: Measured 1TB model state takes ~7-9 minutes to transfer across racks at current network bursts; KV-warmup for long-context models ~10-15s per session. So compaction should target cold sessions and be limited to off-peak.

alex: Suggest we run a 2-week pilot in staging: create 1) insurance-pool (mixed GPUs), 2) compaction-window nightly 02:00-04:00 UTC, 3) soft-affinity scheduler rules, and 4) fragmentation metric in console. If pilot reduces tail evictions by >12% without >5% cost increase, we'll roll to canary in prod for two regions (us-west-2, eu-central-1).

maria: I can owner the pilot dashboard + fragmentation metric. Sam, can you size the initial insurance pool?

sam: I'll run sims. Quick back-of-envelope: we should start with 150 GPUs (mixed) = ~4k hrs/mo buffer. Will post sim outputs by EOD.

capacity-bot: sim run scheduled: command -> `./tools/pack-sim --traffic q4-surge --mix insurance-pool:150 --affinity soft --compaction-window 02:00-04:00`

kai: Also flag: APAC region has lower network egress limits on some colo. If compaction migrates cross-region (bad idea), we'd hit egress cost spike. Keep compaction intra-region; prefer same-az migrations.

jen: Noted. Also need to update SLA docs: explain insurance pool is not guaranteed capacity; enterprises with strict latency need to keep dedicated pins.

alex: Ops checklist for pilot: 1) create pool config, 2) push scheduler change to canary cluster, 3) dashboard + fragmentation metric, 4) run sim + dry-run compaction on staging, 5) run chaos test for eviction scenarios. Who's on it?

maria: I'll take dashboard + fragmentation metric.

sam: I'll run sims + initial pool sizing.

kai: I'll handle scheduler changes + affinity rules.

jen: I'll update SLA blurb + run ksm/network cost calc.

sre-oncall: Ping me when pilot is ready for chaos testing. I want eviction traces and rollback playbook.

alex: Great. Let's reconvene Thu 10:30 PT for go/no-go. Thanks all. :rocket:
